claims.proposition_evaluated: At its August 26, 2026 meeting, the Infrastructure Committee carried a meeting-wide motion reducing each approved speaker's maximum from the five minutes in section 38(1) of Bylaw 18155 to three minutes, and its approved list for bike-lane item 7.6 contained 60 to 80 entries.
claims.interpretation_notes: Supported under the brief's primary definitions: item 2.3 has 64 approved entries for item 7.6. The item 1.4 motion applies to every approved speaker at the meeting, not just item 7.6. Alternative results, holding other choices primary: N = 64 under the 50–90 band, Supported; N-all = 79 under either band, Supported; N-spoke = 52 under the 60–80 band, Partially supported, and under the 50–90 band, Supported. The finding is definition-sensitive because the presentation count changes the row under the primary band. The motion was the third under item 1.4, before Requests to Speak at item 2.3 and before the first item 7.6 speaker; item 2.4 designated 7.6 the first item of business. The minutes record a maximum, not each speaker's actual duration. They record no reason for the cut, speaker positions, or whether registrants were complainants. My round-1 presentation count was wrong; correcting it does not change the primary verdict or any alternative row.

supporting_evidence.finding: Section 38(1) sets a five-minute maximum per approved speaker. Section 4 permits a Standing Committee to modify the bylaw by special resolution, defined in section 2(2)(m) as at least two-thirds of all committee members voting in favour. The consolidation's amendment list and section notes show no post-2022 amendment to section 38 through October 29, 2025.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The standing limit and the required vote for a committee modification.
supporting_evidence.quote: Each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of 5 minutes.

supporting_evidence.finding: Under item 1.4, M. Janz moved a section 38 adjustment for the August 26 meeting: a three-minute maximum for each approved speaker, three minutes for each Council member to ask questions, and three minutes to speak to or close debate on a motion. E. Rutherford, A. Salvador, R. Clarke, M. Janz, A. Knack and A. Paquette voted in favour; the motion carried 6–0.
supporting_evidence.source_publisher: City of Edmonton, Office of the City Clerk
supporting_evidence.establishes: The carried, meeting-wide three-minute limit, its mover, terms and vote.
supporting_evidence.quote: each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of three minutes

supporting_evidence.finding: Item 2.3 approved item 7.6 speakers in five panels of 15, 15, 15, 15 and 4 entries. The total is 64 entries, including 15 with an organization's name. No additional item 7.6 speaker motion appears in the carried minutes.
supporting_evidence.source_publisher: City of Edmonton, Office of the City Clerk
supporting_evidence.establishes: The primary count is inside the stipulated 60–80 band.

supporting_evidence.finding: Sections 9 and 14(4.1) direct the Infrastructure Committee to follow the Council Procedures Bylaw and provide five appointed councillor members; section 15(3) lets the Mayor vote and be counted when present. With the Mayor present, the six votes in favour exceed the four votes required from six members.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The applicable procedures and six-member denominator for the special-resolution calculation.

challenging_evidence.finding: Item 7.6 records presentation panels of 16, 16, 18 and 2 public-speaker entries, totaling 52. Under the alternative definition that counts those recorded as presenting, this falls below the primary 60–80 band, though inside 50–90.
challenging_evidence.source_publisher: City of Edmonton, Office of the City Clerk
challenging_evidence.establishes: The required alternative count makes the finding definition-sensitive.

limitations: On October 2, 2026, my web tool returned 403 for the live post-meeting minutes and 502 for Bylaw 18155. I used the public documents carried in the package for those sources; all reviewers received the same extracts, so agreement on them is not independent retrieval. I read Bylaw 18156 directly from https://www.edmonton.ca/sites/default/files/public-files/documents/bl18156.pdf.
The carried post-meeting minutes show no later correction to items 1.4, 2.3 or 7.6. Their approval or later correction status could not be checked on the live portal.
Counts are entries, not distinct people. Redacted names cannot be matched between approval and presentation lists or across agenda items.

The carried minutes cover selected items, so a search for a City-recorded reason was limited to the carried minutes and agenda. Neither states one. I cannot infer a reason from the queue size or the change in scheduled adjournment.

A web search for earlier section 38 adjustments since October 29, 2025 identified none, but I could not systematically review the portal's meeting minutes. No claim about how unusual this motion was follows from that search.

The agenda and minutes list five public-speaker attachments under item 7.6. Their contents were not supplied; the minutes record no individual speaking durations or extension motion in the carried items.

claims.suggested_one_line: Supported: the Infrastructure Committee voted 6–0 to cut every approved speaker's maximum from five to three minutes for its August 26 meeting, and 64 entries were approved for the bike-lane item.
claims.suggested_short_answer: The Infrastructure Committee, rather than full Council, carried a meeting-wide three-minute speaking limit on August 26, 2026. Its bike-lane item had 64 approved-speaker entries, within the brief's range for “about seventy”; 79 entries were approved across all items. The minutes record 52 entries as presenting on the bike-lane item. Counting presentations instead would put the figure below the primary range, so the finding depends on which list “queue” means. The minutes give no reason for the cut and do not identify speakers' positions.
suggested_tldr: Bylaw 18155 set a five-minute maximum for each approved speaker.
M. Janz's motion set a three-minute maximum for every approved speaker at the meeting; it carried 6–0.
The approved list for item 7.6 had 64 entries; the whole meeting's approved lists had 79.
The minutes record 52 presentation entries for item 7.6, making the range result definition-sensitive.
The minutes do not state why the limit changed or which side speakers supported.
